messages:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Pager: High error rate and node flaps in inference-pool-4 (us-central). Alert: 80% of requests hitting 503s / timeouts over last 3m. Affected service: redwood-infer-runtime. Paging eng-runtime rotation. Incident ID: INC-20260315-089

Maya G: on it. acked the page. @Ajay can you triage kernel or kubelet errors? I'll start customer impact triage and notify CS.

Ajay R: looking at metrics now — node readiness oscillating. grafana shows kubelet restarts on 3 hosts in pool-4 around 22:49 UTC. pod restarts for model-serving containers spiked.

Samir: popping into k8s: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer` shows: 
```
ip-10-0-45-12   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   4d   v1.26.3   10.0.45.12   <none>   inference-pool-4
ip-10-0-45-13   NotReady                2m   v1.26.3   10.0.45.13   <none>   inference-pool-4
ip-10-0-45-14   NotReady                1m   v1.26.3   10.0.45.14   <none>   inference-pool-4
```
Those two NotReady nodes are cycling kubelet restarts. checking kubelet logs...

Ajay R: paste from journalctl on one of the nodes: 
```
Mar 15 22:48:58 ip-10-0-45-14 systemd[1]: Started kubelet: The Kubernetes Node Agent.
Mar 15 22:49:01 ip-10-0-45-14 kubelet[1234]: E0315 22:49:01 kubelet_node_status.go:70] Failed to get node status: timed out waiting for the condition
Mar 15 22:49:02 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 5678 (runc) score 1024 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 22:49:03 docker: container exited with code 137 (OOMKilled)
```

Maya G: OOM + kubelet restart loop. That could be driver/allocator + memory pressure. Tess (CS) — any customer reports?

Tess (CS): yes, two customers reported degraded latency and 503s ~22:50 UTC. Both on high-concurrency endpoints. I'm sending status note to affected accounts.

Samir: container logs from model-serving show repeated CUDA initialization errors before OOM: `E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:906] failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_NO_BINARY_FOR_GPU` and then memory allocations fail. Could be driver mismatch + memory leak under certain batch sizes.

Ajay R: good catch. Also seeing continuous eviction signals: kubelet logs show `eviction manager: memory available below threshold` and system OOM in dmesg. Likely hosts under memory pressure due to a runaway process (maybe a quantized operator allocating pinned pages).

Maya G: mitigation plan proposal (short): 1) cordon the two NotReady/unstable nodes from pool-4 to prevent further scheduling. 2) scale up fallback pool (inference-pool-4-fallback) by +2 nodes and route new traffic there via smart routing. 3) reduce default batching and KV cache size for active model configs to free memory. 4) if nodes remain unstable, autoscaler should replace them — trigger instance replacement. 5) postmortem after stable. Agree?

Samir: +1. I can cordon now and trigger a scale-up. Will also push a quick config to drop batch_size from 8 -> 4 for heavy models (will apply via runtime-configs API).

infra-bot: `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6` (dry-run false) — replacement requested for i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6 in us-central-1a.

Ajay R: while infra replaces, we should shift traffic off the unhealthy nodes immediately. Maya — can you flip the routing policy to prefer fallback pool? Command: `POST /routing/policies/route` with body `{"from":"inference-pool-4","to":"inference-pool-4-fallback","policy":"prefer-fallback","weight":100}`.

Maya G: done. Routing updated. I also notified the Canary monitors to suppress noisy alerts during mitigation.

Samir: cordoned and drained the two nodes: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-13 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30` — pods rescheduled to fallback pool.

Ajay R: quick memory-pressure mitigations applied: reduced batch_size and kv_cache_size for top 3 models. sample config diff: 
```json
{"model":"redwood-13b","batch_size":4,"kv_cache_mb":512}
```
Applied via `redwoodctl apply-config`.

Tess (CS): relaying to customers that traffic is being routed to fallback pool and we expect reduced latency but lower concurrency until nodes are replaced. Customers acknowledged, thanks.

Samir: infra reports node replacement in progress; new instances booting with kernel 5.15.0 and nvidia-driver 525. Tried to repro on staging — we saw similar OOM when batch_size>=8 + long-lived KV cache. Suspect a memory regression in recent runtime change that touched allocator behavior.

Ajay R: can we revert the recent allocator tweak from yesterday's deploy? That would remove one variable.

Maya G: yes — rolling revert queued for canary only for now. We'll watch for stability and then roll further.

infra-bot: replaced instance i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6 -> i-0f6e5d4c3b2a1. New node joined pool and reports Ready at 22:56 UTC.

Samir: after routing and config changes, error rate dropped to baseline in the last 3m. No new OOMs in logs on the new nodes.

Maya G: great. keeping the incident open for monitoring + postmortem. Action items:
- Samir to collect kubelet/journal logs and container OOM traces and attach to incident workspace.
- Ajay to run bisection on allocator change and stage revert results.
- Infra to verify driver + kernel image across pool (ensure consistency).
- Tess to complete customer follow-ups and finalize incident comms.

Samir: capturing logs now. gist: https://internal-gists/redwood/incident-2210004321-logs (privileged).

Tess (CS): sent out interim update to affected customers. will send final note after postmortem.

Maya G: thanks team. marking pager resolved in PD, leaving thread for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260315-089 status: Resolved (mitigation in place). Time to resolve: ~14m. Link to incident runbook: https://internal/runbooks/inference-node-flap
